messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up to the kernel-selection / attention-opt RFC. Proposing a small runtime-facing abstraction called KernelAdapter that exposes: a compact capability bitmask (SM features, tensor core levels, fp8 support), a fast probe API, and a pure function preferred_kernel(model_shape, quant_mode, sm_caps) -> kernel_tag. Goal: let serving select precompiled or JIT kernels reliably across A100/H100/L4 while keeping probe cost negligible and ABI stable. Thoughts?

Raj: +1 on an adapter. Main worry: probe cost and frequency. We can't run a heavyweight probe on every container start in multi-tenant nodes. Need a caching layer (node-level) and a TTL. Also watch for driver/firmware changes invalidating cache.

Sasha: did some numbers on real HW with the current probe prototype: A100 / H100 / L4. Summary: A100 prefers fused-attn kernel for seq<=1024 (median 12.3ms), H100 picks tensor-int8 path for seq>2048 (median 9.8ms), L4 falls back to fp16 kernel (median 18.5ms). Cold probe cost ~45ms (compiling/probing), cached probe ~2ms. So caching is critical.

probe-bot: automated bench @1834125800 posted: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/bench/1834125800 (contains csv of per-shape latencies + env tags).

Raj: Another angle: per-shape preferences. The adapter must return preferences scoped by (seq_len_bucket, batch_size, quant_mode). One flat kernel_tag isn't enough. Also need an API like is_compatible(kernel_tag, model_metadata) to avoid selecting kernels that break KV cache layout.

Maya: Agreed on per-shape mapping. Design idea: preferred_kernel returns an ordered list of kernel_tags with a score. If top choice fails at runtime, fallback to next. Keep the function pure (no side effects) so tests are deterministic.

Linus: From ops: do not let probe delay pod readiness. Suggest probing at node boot via an init daemon and writing node annotation (/var/lib/redwood/probe_cache or k8s node label). Runtime adapter does a cheap cache lookup; if missing it uses a super-conservative probe (only checks a tiny microkernel) that costs <5ms.

Sasha: Also see mixed-workload problem: same GPU pool may serve short chat sessions and long-context generation. Routing by seq_len histogram should live in the serving router that calls KernelAdapter per-request, not in the adapter itself. Adapter stays declarative: "these are the ranked kernels for this shape".

Raj: ABI stability: precompiled bundles need qualification fields: driver_hash, cuda_version, cudnn_hash, and sm_capabilities bitmask. Probe results must include those so we invalidate cache when any change occurs.

Maya: Good call. Telemetry: collection must be minimal but useful. Proposed fields: k (kernel_tag), s (seq_len), b (batch_size), l (latency_ms), f (fallback_reason or empty). Keep telemetry schema tiny for high-cardinality workloads.

Linus: Rollout plan: feature flag on dedicated pools, canary for 5% traffic for 7 days. Success criteria: P95 latency regressions <5% and cost-per-token decrease >=10%. If we detect repeated fallbacks (>1%) escalate to automatic rollback.

Sasha: Implementation TODOs I will own: 1) Spec doc for KernelAdapter API (methods + wire format for probe results), 2) probe daemon + cache schema, 3) serving-router hook points + example pseudocode, 4) telemetry labels and lightweight schema. Drafting PR & spec today.

Raj: I'll review the cache invalidation semantics and the driver-hash rules. Also will prototype a tiny atomic update path for node-local cache to avoid thundering herd.

Linus: I'll add the rollout checklist and the telemetry dashboards we need before canary. Ops will also add an init-container probe image to the node bootstrap repo.

Maya: Perfect. Sasha please post the spec link when ready and tag Raj/Linus. We'll aim to merge the adapter interface and a non-blocking probe daemon behind a feature flag in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
